Twenty-two comments

Eileen O’Callaghan’s

Sorry I can’t remember where I first learned this tasty little reel, but it was directly off a live player. I’ve note heard this tune played very widely, though it does crop up at sessions now and then.

I learned it as a single reel, played ABAB, and at a moderate pace. It fits well with reels in D major, but I also like to follow it with Eileen Curran in G dorian--the symmetry of the Eileen twins comes through in the titles and certain phrases in the melodies.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on December 16th, 2002.

There are a few different names for this tune, and it sometimes gets played in A.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on December 17th, 2002.

I play it in this key - nice tune

Eileen O’Callaghan’s

I’m glad to hear that other people are playing this. In the spirit of recent discussions about improving our posting of tunes, here’s a more basic setting of the tune.

L: 1/8
R: reel
K: Gmaj

Sister tune

There are many tunes related to this reel, including “Trim the Velvet,” “Kiss the Maid behind the Barrel,” “The Steampacket,” etc. But the closest one is probably “the Milliner’s Daughter”: https://thesession.org/tunes/1409

↳ Posted by slainte on May 7th, 2006.

Original setting?

I’ve added #5 from an old 78 of the Aughrim Slopes Ceilidhe Band, featured on the CD Past Masters of Irish Dance Music; also the spelling “Geoghegan’s” from the Joe Burke/Michael Cooney LP, to add to the ever growing pile of variants of the name. Burke and Cooney play this setting, perhaps the old record popularized this reel, or it’s a Galway tune.

↳ Posted by Lucy Rietmann on December 31st, 2012.

Eileen O’Callaghan’s, X:6 - Peter Carberry’s

‘Peter Carberry’s’ as played by Angelina on ‘Pluckin’ Mad‘ is very close to this reel - ’Eileen O‘Callaghan’s’ though the second part is slightly different. I think they’re probably close enough to be variants of the one tune.
